processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cold rolling is a necessary step to change the grain structure, grain size and texture in ferritic low density steels; a fully recrystallized microstructure can be obtained after final recrystallization annealing following a 50% cold rolling reduction in a Fe-7%Al steel [41].

The ferritic Fe-Al steels are generally cold rolled and heated to 700–1000 °C for recrystallization annealing to control the grain size and texture of the ferrite matrix as well as the precipitation of κ-carbides, applying the continuous annealing line used for conventional HSLA steel strips (b0105). A fully recrystallized microstructure is obtained after final recrystallization annealing within 700–950 °C following a 50% cold rolling reduction in a Fe-7%Al steel (b0114).

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase δ-ferrite matrix, fully recrystallized after cold rolling plus recrystallization annealing; δ-ferrite grains become more or less equiaxed with a random texture (relatively higher intensity of the Cube fibre). As Al not only extends the ferrite region to high temperatures but also raises the recrystallization temperature of ferrite, the δ-ferrite grain size cannot be sufficiently refined during hot rolling, so cold rolling and annealing are required; the δ-ferrite is the phase directly produced from the liquid.

phases_present.crystal_structure: BCC (ordered/disordered: A2-disordered FeAl, B2-ordered FeAl or DO3-ordered Fe3Al depending on Al content)
phases_present.morphology: more or less equiaxed after recrystallization annealing
phases_present.texture: random, with relatively higher intensity of the Cube fibre {001}<110>

grain_structure.texture: random with relatively higher intensity of the Cube fibre {001}<110>

precipitates.distribution: coarse κ-carbides can be formed along the original δ-ferrite grain boundaries if the cooling rate is slow; precipitation of κ-carbides may also occur during recrystallization annealing

interfaces.phase_evolution: In the ferritic Fe-Al matrix the δ-ferrite is directly produced from liquid; there is no γ↔α transformation over the process temperature range, so the ferrite matrix is retained through cold rolling and annealing while κ-carbides may precipitate.
interfaces.interface_notes: In the α (BCC) phase the lattice parameter of the κ phase is 0.387–0.389 nm and α/κ interfaces are semicoherent (lattice mismatch 6% [59]); in the ferritic matrix κ-carbides are present as semicoherent precipitates with thick, elongated rod-like shape, in contrast to the nanoscale cuboidal coherent κ-carbides found in austenitic Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Fe-6.8Al and Fe-8.1Al ferritic Fe-Al steels after recrystallization annealing at 850 °C for 5 min (Fig. 26); tensile properties of Fe-Al ferritic alloys reported to be comparable with HSLA steels.

youngs_modulus.value: 2–2.5% reduction in Young's modulus per 1 wt% Al addition (polycrystalline Fe-Al alloys, annealed state, room temperature); α-Fe 207 GPa

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curves of cold rolled and annealed Fe-6.8Al and Fe-8.1Al steels (Fig. 26)

strain_hardening_rate.value: strain hardening exponent n = 0.19–0.21 (for Al in the range 6–9%)
